To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) scattering functions at specific scattering angles and wavelengths contain sufficient information to invert the aerosol particle size distribution, (2) a set of scattering functions combined with extinction coefficients is less sensitive to inaccuracies of the refractive index, but the inversion range is smaller, and (3) errors in the experimental data of up to 8%, in terms of the scattering functions and extinction coefficient, are acceptable for inversion.

the scattering functions at specific scattering angles and wavelengths and extinction coefficients at specific wavelengths contain sufficient information to allow inversion of the particle size distribution in the 0-40 microm radius range with errors of less than 20%.
the information content of aerosol scattering functions is sufficient for inversion of the particle size distribution in the 0-40-micron range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the information content of aerosol size distribution with respect to the optical parameters of the scattering and extinction coefficients.
the information content in optical data and the influence of errors in the experimental data on the inversion results.
the information content of optical data with respect to the aerosol size distributions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the information content in aerosol optical data is sufficient to determine the aerosol size distributions, if one uses scattering functions and extinction coefficient data at different wavelengths and scattering angles, and if the inversion is performed with an appropriate numerical algorithm.
a set of scattering functions measured at specific wavelengths and angles is the optimum set for aerosol size distribution retrieval.
a set of scattering functions and an extinction coefficient at a single wavelength is sufficient to obtain a good inversion result.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scattering functions of the particles are the main information source for the inversion.
the scattering functions are the most important parameters to measure, and that the information content of these data is not very sensitive to the choice of scattering angle.
the aerosol optical properties contain sufficient information to retrieve the size distribution of the particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information content of aerosol scattering functions and extinction coefficient with respect to the particle size distribution can be used to optimize the design of future measurement campaigns.
the inversion algorithm is not very sensitive to small variations of the optical data, but it is very sensitive to the assumed refractive index.
the scattering function is a more sensitive optical parameter than the extinction coefficient.
